chunks: My father and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-‘Aṭṭār, from Ḥamdān ibn Sulaymān al-Naysābūrī, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad al-Yamānī, from Manī‘ ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Yūnus ibn ‘Abd al-Raḥmān, from Ṣafwān al-Jammāl, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man leaves his house intending to visit al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), seven hundred angels will accompany him from above his head, below him, to his right, to his left, in front of him, and behind him until they bring him to his safe haven. When he visits al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), a caller will announce to him, 'You have been forgiven, so resume your deeds.' Then they will return with him, accompanying him back to his house. When they arrive at his house, they will say, 'We entrust you to Allah.' They will continue visiting him until the day of his death, and then they will visit the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) every day, and the reward of that will be for the man.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward and angelic accompaniment for visiting the shrine of Imam al-Husain?
ai.summary: In *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Ibn Qulawayh highlights the cosmological significance of Ziyarat al-Husayn, portraying it not merely as a physical journey but as a celestial event where the visitor is enveloped by seven hundred angels from all directions. This continuous divine accompaniment until death underscores the enduring spiritual merit of the pilgrimage, linking the earthly act of visiting the shrine with eternal reward and divine forgiveness.
